structure.description: Top-level directory for reusable React UI components used throughout the app. Houses feature-agnostic, presentational components such as the Calculator. Future shared primitives (Button, Input, Card, Modal) would also live here once the app grows beyond a single feature.

Folder for the Calculator feature component. Contains the main Calculator component implementation and its colocated CSS Module stylesheet. No sub-folders are needed because the component has no internal sub-components — the history line, display, and keypad grid are all rendered inline from a single button-layout data array.

Main calculator component implementing the four basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), plus the standard +/- sign toggle and percent (%) helpers to make the calculator feel complete. Default-exported React FC, takes no props. State (all useState, fully local to this component): - currentInput: string — the value currently shown on the main display, initialized to '0'. - previousValue: number | null — the first stored operand, null until an operator is pressed. - operator: '+' | '-' | 'x' | '/' | null — the pending operator, null until one is pressed. - waitingForOperand: boolean — true after an operator or equals has just been pressed, indicating that the next digit press should replace currentInput rather than append to it. - lastPressedWasEquals: boolean — true immediately after '=' so the next digit press starts a fresh calculation instead of continuing from the result. Helpers (private, defined inside the component file): - formatDisplay(value: number): string — converts a numeric result to a compact display string using Number(value.toPrecision(12)) then .toString() to avoid floating-point artifacts (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 → 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004), and returns 'Error' when the value is not finite (NaN or Infinity, including the division-by-zero case). - calculate(a: number, b: number, op: Operator): number — returns the result of applying op to a and b; division by zero returns NaN so formatDisplay can render 'Error'. Event handlers: - inputDigit(digit: string) — if waitingForOperand or lastPressedWasEquals is true, replace currentInput with the digit and clear both flags; otherwise append the digit but only if the resulting length stays under ~12 characters. - inputDecimal() — if waitingForOperand is true, start a new '0.' input; otherwise insert '.' only when currentInput does not already contain one. - performOperation(nextOperator: Operator) — if previousValue and operator are both set (chained operation), compute the pending result first via calculate, store the new value into previousValue, then set the new operator and waitingForOperand; otherwise just store the parsed currentInput into previousValue and set waitingForOperand. Always updates the operator to nextOperator. - handleEquals() — if previousValue and operator are set, compute the final result, set currentInput to formatDisplay(result), clear previousValue and operator, and set lastPressedWasEquals to true. - handleClear() — resets all state to defaults: currentInput '0', previousValue null, operator null, waitingForOperand false, lastPressedWasEquals false. - toggleSign() — multiplies the parsed current input by -1 and updates currentInput via formatDisplay; no-op if currentInput is '0' or 'Error'. - handlePercent() — divides the parsed current input by 100 and updates currentInput via formatDisplay; no-op if currentInput is 'Error'. Keyboard support (useEffect on mount, cleanup on unmount): - A single window keydown listener maps '0'–'9' to inputDigit, '.' to inputDecimal, '+' to performOperation('+'), '-' to performOperation('-'), '*' to performOperation('x'), '/' to performOperation('/'), 'Enter' or '=' to handleEquals, 'Escape' or 'Delete' to handleClear, and 'Backspace' to remove the last character of currentInput (no-op when waitingForOperand is true, lastPressedWasEquals is true, or currentInput is 'Error'). - The listener ignores events whose target is an INPUT, TEXTAREA, or contenteditable element so it remains a good citizen on pages that add form fields later. Rendered UI structure (all inside a single
): - A history line
{previousValue !== null && operator ? `${formatDisplay(previousValue)} ${operator}` : '\u00A0'}
showing the pending operand and operator when one is set (uses a non-breaking space as a placeholder so the row keeps its reserved height). - A main display
{currentInput}
, large, right-aligned, monospaced, with overflow handling. - A keypad container
holding buttons generated from a local const BUTTON_LAYOUT: {label, kind, value, ariaLabel, span?}[] iterated with .map. The 4x5 layout: Row 1: AC (action), +/- (action), % (action), ÷ (operator) Row 2: 7 (digit), 8 (digit), 9 (digit), × (operator) Row 3: 4 (digit), 5 (digit), 6 (digit), − (operator) Row 4: 1 (digit), 2 (digit), 3 (digit), + (operator) Row 5: 0 (digit, span: 2), . (digit), = (equals) - Each button is a real

CSS Module styles for the Calculator component. Uses the global design tokens already declared in src/index.css (--text, --text-h, --bg, --border, --code-bg, --accent, --accent-bg, --accent-border, --social-bg, --shadow, --mono) and defines two local tokens at the top of the file: --radius-md: 12px and --radius-lg: 16px. All other spacing, colors, and typography values reference the global tokens to keep the calculator visually consistent with the rest of the app's design language.

Key rules:
- .calculator: flex column container, background var(--bg), border 1px solid var(--border), border-radius var(--radius-lg), box-shadow var(--shadow), padding 20px, max-width 340px, width 100%, margin 40px auto, box-sizing border-box, user-select none (to avoid text selection on rapid clicks).
- .history: min-height 1.2em (so layout doesn't jump when content appears/disappears), text-align right, color var(--text), opacity 0.7, font-family var(--mono), font-size 14px, padding 0 8px, overflow hidden, text-overflow ellipsis, white-space nowrap.
- .display: text-align right, color var(--text-h), font-family var(--mono), font-size 44px, font-weight 300, letter-spacing -0.5px, font-variant-numeric tabular-nums, line-height 1.1, padding 12px 8px 24px, overflow hidden, text-overflow ellipsis, white-space nowrap, min-height 1.2em.
- .keypad: display grid, grid-template-columns repeat(4, 1fr), gap 10px.
- .btn (base button): display flex, align-items center, justify-content center, height 64px, border-radius var(--radius-md), border 1px solid transparent, background transparent, font-family var(--mono), font-size 22px, color inherit, cursor pointer, transition background 120ms ease, transform 80ms ease, outline none, user-select none. :hover { filter: brightness(0.96); }. :active { transform: scale(0.97); filter: brightness(0.92); }. :focus-visible { outline 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset 2px; }.
- .btn.digit: background var(--code-bg); color var(--text-h); font-weight 400.
- .btn.operator: background var(--accent-bg); color var(--accent); font-weight 500.
- .btn.action: background var(--social-bg); color var(--text); font-size 18px (slightly smaller for AC/+/-/% to visually de-emphasize them vs digits).
- .btn.equals: background var(--accent); color var(--bg); font-weight 600; font-size 24px.
- .btn[data-value='0']: grid-column span 2; text-align left; padding-left 24px (so the 0 visually aligns with the leftmost column of the other digits in the same row).
- Responsive (@media max-width: 420px): .calculator { margin: 16px; padding 16px; }. .btn { height 56px; font-size 20px; }. .display { font-size 36px; }. .keypad { gap 8px; }.
- Accessibility: focus ring is implemented via :focus-visible (not :focus) so mouse users don't see an outline on every click but keyboard users always do.

modifiedFiles.description: Replaces the Vite template body (the counter button, hero image, and logo SVGs) with a clean rendering of the new Calculator component. The component function is reduced to simply returning <Calculator />, and the now-unused imports (useState from 'react', reactLogo, viteLogo, heroImg from './assets/*', and the './App.css' stylesheet) are removed. The default export 'App' and the file's location are preserved so main.tsx continues to mount the app without changes. The unused template asset files (src/assets/react.svg, src/assets/vite.svg, src/assets/hero.png) and src/App.css are intentionally left on disk; this task does not require cleaning up template files.
modifiedFiles.reason: App.tsx now mounts the Calculator component in place of the Vite template

notes: tsconfig.app.json does not declare a 'paths' alias for '@/*' and vite.config.ts does not define resolve.alias, so all imports use relative paths (e.g. './components/Calculator').

tsconfig.app.json sets 'verbatimModuleSyntax: true', so any future type-only imports must be written as 'import type { ... }' rather than 'import { ... }'. The current Calculator has no external type imports, so this is informational only.

The Calculator is implemented as a single component rather than split into Display, Keypad, and Button sub-components because the request is for a simple calculator and over-componentizing one cohesive UI would add import complexity without reuse benefit. The render-structure section of the description still calls out each region (history, display, keypad grid) so the implementation is unambiguous.

Keyboard support (digits, operators, Enter, Backspace, Escape) is included in the description because a basic calculator that ignores keyboard input feels unprofessional; it can be omitted by the implementation agent if a keyboard-less version is preferred, but it is recommended for the UX quality directive.

Design tokens are consumed from the existing global --* variables in src/index.css and from two locally-defined radius tokens inside Calculator.module.css. A separate src/styles/tokens.css was not scaffolded because the app currently has only one component; the global index.css already provides color, typography, and shadow tokens, and lifting the local radius tokens into a shared file is recommended only when a second component needs them.
The unused template assets (src/assets/react.svg, src/assets/vite.svg, src/assets/hero.png) and src/App.css are intentionally left on disk because the task did not request cleanup of template files.
